cover.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: original 16:9 editorial cover for an accessible science review of chiral amplification, the nonlinear effects of Kagan and asymmetric autocatalysis of Soai.
Primary request: create a striking sculptural woodcut and embossed-paper still life of handedness becoming predominant through feedback. Two small three-dimensional ribbon helices of the same material wind in opposite handed directions near the start of a single broad curving stream. Along the stream one winding form becomes visibly predominant through repeated sculptural motifs. The stream bends back toward the source in a large open return curve, suggesting a product helping to create more of its own form. The two initial helices must read as opposite windings, not just different colours. Keep this one coherent scene with a clear focal event and generous uncluttered space.
Style and medium: tactile hand-cut woodblock print combined with low embossed-paper relief, crisp expressive cuts, restrained rough ink grain and physical shadows. A quiet but dramatic editorial artwork. Deep midnight-blue ground, ivory relief, copper-rust accents and a little muted sage. Distinguish the two handed forms through their winding geometry and shadow as well as colour.
Composition: wide landscape 16:9. Keep the paired helices, returning stream and the emergence of the predominant form within the central safe area, readable as a 320x180 thumbnail. The repeated modules are abstract geometric sculptures; they do not encode a measured population, a chemical bond structure or an actual reaction vessel.
Constraints: no letters, numbers, equations, labels, axes, logos or watermarks. No human hands, portraits, Nobel medal, robot, brain, circuit board or sci-fi glow. No atom-ball molecular model, no laboratory apparatus, no imitation of a named artist or publication. Opaque background.

cover.prompt:
Final cover v3: built-in image_gen. Exact model identifier not retained. No external artwork was an image-generation input.

Generation
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset: original wide 16:9 editorial illustration for a serious but welcoming science essay about chiral amplification and asymmetric autocatalysis.

A quietly astonishing ceramic scene: a large, beautifully modelled terracotta RIGHT HAND gently cups, supports and shapes a new ivory RIGHT HAND from a small mound of soft clay. Both sculptures are unambiguously right hands, with five anatomically coherent digits and matching thumb positions. The emerging hand is almost complete, still joined at its wrist to the unformed clay, and its fingertips begin to support a new small fold of clay. No outside sculptor is present: what was made is becoming the maker. Focus on the tender physical junction between a finished fingertip and the new clay thumb. This is a sculptural metaphor, not living skin or a biological transformation.

Compose the hands as one graceful asymmetrical, interlocking gesture viewed obliquely, not a pair of hands facing each other on a desk. Keep a subtle shallow LEFT-HAND impression in the clay at the lower periphery, representing the other mirror possibility. The two right hands dominate the action; the opposite impression is quiet. No rows or grid and no heap of miniature hands. A continuous handmade paper-like clay surface joins the scene and opens into generous negative space.

Art direction: sophisticated hand-painted gouache, lithographic grain and tactile clay sculpture. Broad confident shapes, strong silhouette, carefully chosen few edges, warm dusty terracotta and pale chalk ivory against a muted deep blue-green ground. A hint of soft rose in reflected light. Intimate, humane, contemplative and curious. Avoid photographic disembodied limbs, uncanny skin, body horror, clinical blue gloves, glossy CGI, stock-art sentimentality or ornate decoration. A poetic artwork whose meaning is discovered through the physical action, not a scientific diagram. Independent composition and no imitation of any existing artwork.
No text, equations, labels, arrows, atom models, apparatus, medals, logos or watermark. Opaque background.

Same clay and palm anatomy
Edit this original clay-hand illustration. Preserve its broad interlocking gesture, intimate point of contact, deep blue-green painterly ground, gouache texture, quiet right-side negative space and overall lighting.

Resolve the scientific metaphor by changing the following together:
1. BOTH SCULPTURES must be the SAME anatomical LEFT HAND, shown clearly from the PALM SIDE. Each has five coherent digits, four fingers and one opposable thumb. The palm crease and thumb base must be readable. With each hand considered upright, both thumbs are on the viewer's RIGHT and four fingers fan to the viewer's LEFT. In particular rebuild the small hand with its thumb on the RIGHT edge, its long index finger on the LEFT side, and coherent palm anatomy. Both hands can curl gently toward the shared focal point; preserve their same handedness. No fingernails on the palm-facing surfaces.
2. Both hands are made from the SAME warm ivory, unfired ceramic clay, with the same tool marks and ochre shadows. The larger hand is a completed clay sculpture, not a living person's orange hand. Show its short blunt sculpted wrist base fully INSIDE the composition, resting on the clay surface, so there is no external human arm entering from the picture edge.
3. The completed clay hand supports and shapes the nearly completed second hand, which rises at its wrist from a SEPARATE mound of unformed clay. The new hand's finger lightly touches a fresh tiny clay curl, suggesting that the result is beginning to help the next act of making. Keep this one tactile encounter dominant, not a pile of hands or repeated miniatures.
4. Remove the ambiguous mirror-hand imprint in the foreground; replace it with a few subtle tool marks and open breathing space.

Make the complete picture feel like a crafted, humane and thought-provoking ceramic allegory. Gentle warm highlights, broad painted forms and material depth. Preserve the non-photographic medium and calm, artful restraint. No human skin, blood, wounds, severed-arm imagery, clinical objects, text, numbers, symbols, arrows, labels, logos or watermarks. Opaque background.

Small-hand reflection
Make ONE local geometric edit to this illustration. Preserve the entire large clay hand exactly, its pose, its base, all lighting, the blue-green ground, the clay mounds, painterly surface, framing and negative space.
Horizontally MIRROR ONLY THE SMALL HAND, from its wrist upward, keeping it an anatomically coherent five-digit palm. Its thumb and thumb mound must now be on the VIEWER'S LEFT of its palm; the four long fingers must fan to the VIEWER'S RIGHT. Clearly show palm creases and no palm-side fingernails. Mirror the WHOLE small hand geometry as one unit, not just a displaced thumb. The small hand remains connected at its wrist to the same clay mound. Adjust its highest fingertip contact locally so it lightly touches the clay curl held by the large hand. Both sculptures remain made from the same warm ivory unfired clay.
The large grasping sculpture is a right hand; this local mirror makes the small sculpture a right hand too. Preserve the complete large hand without reshaping it. Do not mirror the canvas or background. No added digits, hands, labels, text, marks or objects. Opaque background.

Extra digit correction
Correct ONE small anatomical error in the smaller clay hand only. Keep all other pixels and composition as close as possible.
The small palm-facing hand currently has a thumb at the viewer's LEFT plus FIVE long finger protrusions. Remove ONLY the EXTRA, farthest-RIGHT shortest protrusion (approximately x=1125,y=425 in this 1672x941 image). Smooth that one outer silhouette into the right edge of the palm. The finished smaller hand must have exactly FIVE DIGITS TOTAL: one thumb on the viewer's left and FOUR long fingers, with their four tips around x=900,985,1045,1090. Preserve the established RIGHT-HAND palm anatomy, palm creases, highest fingertip contact and clay texture.
Do not remove any of the other four fingers. Do not add or move digits. Keep the large hand completely unchanged, same clay, base, contact, backgrounds, lighting, colours and framing. No text, arrows, marks or watermark. Opaque background.
